title: The Evolving Threat of Deepfakes
summary: Deepfakes are synthetic media that can be incredibly convincing and are getting more sophisticated as technology advances. They can take many forms, including audio, video, and image content, and can be used to spread misinformation or create fake content for malicious purposes. The prevalence of deepfakes is increasing, with a 400% increase in deepfake sexual content between 2022 and 2023.

So what are deepfakes? Deepfakes can take many forms of encompassing audio, video and image content, often they involve showing a real person doing or saying something that they're not. However, they can also depict entirely fictional characters and may be absent of people altogether, so they might present staged events such as a fake image of a battlefield in a war zone. While some deepfakes consist of wholly new novel content, others take the form of existing content that has been manipulated, so where a real video has been edited to manipulate a person's mouth movements and dubbed audio has been added in.

evidence_pool.speaker: Jessica Rose Smith
evidence_pool.text: Embedding involves attaching contextual information to synthetic media through tools like watermarks and labels. Many organizations have started to sign up to various content provenance and authenticity schemes. Detection encompasses efforts to distinguish real from fake content. One means of detecting deepfakes is by using machine learning classifiers that have been trained on known deepfake content. And finally enforcement involves setting clear rules about the types of synthetic content that are allowed to be created and shared on online services. It also requires acting against users that breach these rules for example through suspending or removing user accounts. All of the above interventions show promise and helping to mitigate the creation and spread of harmful deepfakes. But it's important to acknowledge their limitations and weak spots.
